To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Wnt signalling regulates the Snail1 transcription factor by engaging an Axin2–Snail1–GSK3 axis, which is critical for the induction of an EMT-like programme in breast cancer cells.
the Wnt–Axn2–GSK-3β–Snai1 axis is an essential regulator of the epithelial– mesenchymal transition and tumour cell invasiveness.
the Wnt–Ax2–GSKβ cascade is a critical regulator of Snail1 activity, which controls breast cancer cell invasion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms by Wnt signalling regulates epithelial–mesenchemal transition (EMTs) and tissue-invasive programmes in human cancer cells.
the mechanisms by which Wnt signalling induces epithelial–mesen- chymal transition ( EMT ) in human breast cancer cells.

understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate the development of the epithelial to mesenchymal transition, a process that is associated with the development of cancer and the spread of tumour cells from their primary site to distant sites in the body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Wnt signalling induces the EMT through the Axin2–Snail1 pathway.
the Wnt–Axing2–GSK-3β–Snai1 cascade regulates breast cancer cell dedifferentiation.
the Axin2-GSK3β-Snail1 axis is a key regulator of EMT and cancer progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the canonical Wnt signalling pathway engages tumour cell EMT through a GSK3β-dependent mechanism that stabilizes Snail1 protein.
the Wnt signalling pathway is a key regulator of Snail1 activity and that this activity is mediated through the regulation of Snail1 protein stability by Axin2 and GSK3β.
Axin2 acts as an E3 ligase for GSK3b and that the Axin2-GSK3b complex is a nucleocytoplamic chaperone for the Snail1 transcription factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Wnt–β-catenin signalling regulates EMT through a novel pathway that involves the nucleocytoplasm shuttling of Axin2 and GSK3β to stabilize the Snail1 transcriptional repressor.
Wnt signalling engages Snail1 activity through a GSK3β-dependent pathway.
the Wnt–Snail1–EMT axis is a critical regulator of the tissue-invasive behaviour of breast cancer cells.
